content:
For years, Apple has been adding more customization options to iOS. iOS 16 reintroduced full lock screen personalization, iOS 18 added icon color tinting, iOS 26 introduced translucent icons, and iOS 27 brings a full-screen Liquid Glass slider.

Expanding iPhone personalization is a good thing. Now that you can tint your home screen icons, why not extend that capability across the entire operating system?

iOS 27 hasn't even shipped yet, so thinking about what Apple might do in the next software version at this point may be premature. That said, I think a themed application color, beyond Light and Dark Mode, would be a logical next step.

Basically, I want to recreate the Material You aesthetic on iOS — but based on icon color rather than wallpaper — though Apple should also offer a wallpaper-based option. Apple first introduced the option to match icons to a MagSafe case color last year, and a theming system like this would pair well with it.

It's worth noting that Apple already introduced color theming for its integrated development environment, Xcode, earlier this year at WWDC. There are a lot of great choices there — why not bring that fun to the iPhone? Even on the Mac, users can now set system-level tints for third-party apps.

Summary

Overall, I think bringing color theming to iOS would be a great move, and another big step in giving users more room to customize.

What do you think about bringing color theming to iOS and iPadOS? Let us know in the comments.
